home.headline: Selling into Germany? Three obligations most foreign brands are ==missing==.
home.lede: If you ship to German consumers, specific German requirements apply to you — whether or not you have a company here. Most foreign brands we look at are missing at least two of the three below.

obligations.heading: An accessible online shop
obligations.text: Your shop, checkout and customer account have to be usable by people with disabilities, measured against the European standard {de|EN 301 549}. You also need a published accessibility statement. Since January 2026 the German market surveillance authority has been running its own checks, not only responding to complaints.

obligations.heading: A responsible person inside the EU
obligations.law: General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) — applies since 13 December 2024
obligations.text: You may not sell a product to an EU consumer unless a named person or company inside the EU is responsible for it, and their details appear with the product. No EU responsible person means the product cannot lawfully be placed on the market.

obligations.heading: Packaging registered before your first parcel
obligations.law: {de|Verpackungsgesetz} — LUCID registration, required before you sell
obligations.text: Every box, filler and label you send into Germany has to be registered in the {de|LUCID} register and licensed with a dual system. Registration is required _before_ the first shipment, and marketplaces are obliged to block sellers who have not done it.

legal.title: Privacy policy
legal.metaDescription: What personal data elbebridge collects, why, on what legal basis, and what rights you have under the GDPR.
legal.intro: How we handle personal data under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Last updated 15 August 2026.

blocks.text: The controller for the processing described here is:

This website sets no cookies, embeds no third-party scripts and runs no analytics. Nothing about your visit is used to profile you or to advertise to you. That is why you are not being asked to accept anything.

items.desc: Your email address and whatever you choose to put in the message — normally a store URL and a company name.
To run the requested check and reply to you with the result.
Article 6(1)(b) GDPR — steps taken at your request before entering into a contract.
There is no form and no form provider. Your message goes straight to our mailbox, which is hosted by Google Workspace (Google Ireland Limited) as our processor under a data processing agreement.
Twelve months after our last contact, unless you become a client, in which case statutory retention periods for business correspondence apply.

This site is hosted on GitHub Pages, operated by GitHub, Inc. Their servers record standard access log data: IP address, date and time, the page requested, and the browser identifier your browser sends. We have no access to those logs and build no profile from them.
To deliver the site and to keep it secure and available.
Article 6(1)(f) GDPR — our legitimate interest in operating a secure website.
Retention is governed by GitHub's own privacy statement, which you can read at [docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

sections.heading: 5. What we look at when we scan a website

blocks.text: Our scan reads publicly available pages of the website you ask us to check. We record company identification only — the legal entity, its registered address and its registration numbers, as published in that site's own legal notice. We do not log in, we do not place orders, we do not access anything behind authentication, and we do not collect details of named individuals. Our scanner respects {de|robots.txt}, identifies itself in its user agent, and makes at most one request per second.

Two of our processors are reachable from the United States. GitHub, Inc. hosts this website and is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; it also offers Standard Contractual Clauses. Google Workspace is contracted through Google Ireland Limited, with the same frameworks in place for any onward transfer. We tell you this rather than claiming everything stays in Europe, because it does not.
Under the GDPR you have the right to:

items: access the personal data we hold about you (Article 15);
receive it in a portable format (Article 20);
object to processing based on legitimate interest (Article 21).

blocks.text: To exercise any of these, write to [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com). You do not need to give a reason and it costs you nothing.

You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority. The competent authority for us is the {de|Hamburgische Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit} (Hamburg Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information).
If we change how we handle data, we update this page and the date at the top. We keep previous versions on file.

legal.title: Accessibility statement
legal.metaDescription: How accessible this website is, how we tested it, and how to tell us if something does not work for you.
legal.intro: We ask other companies about their accessibility statement, so here is ours. This statement covers the website at elbebridge.com and was last reviewed on 15 August 2026.

blocks.text: We believe this site conforms to {de|EN 301 549} and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 at level AA. Specifically:

items: every page works with the keyboard alone, and the focus indicator is always visible;
the site ships no JavaScript at all, so nothing depends on scripts loading;
text contrast exceeds the required ratio, and nothing is signalled by colour alone;
text can be resized to 200% without loss of content or horizontal scrolling;
the page structure uses real headings and landmarks, in order;
German terms inside English sentences carry their own language attribute, so a screen reader pronounces them correctly.

blocks.text: Automated testing with axe-core against the WCAG 2.2 AA and {de|EN 301 549} rule sets — the same scan we run for clients — followed by manual testing: keyboard-only navigation with the mouse unplugged, and a screen reader pass with NVDA.

Automated tools detect only a minority of accessibility problems. We say this on our own statement for the same reason we say it in every report we write: a clean automated scan is not a claim of accessibility.
None currently recorded. If we become aware of a barrier we cannot fix immediately, we will list it here with a date by which we expect to fix it.

sections.heading: Tell us if something does not work

blocks.text: If you find a barrier on this site, email [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com) and tell us what you were trying to do. We reply within five working days. If you need information from this site in a different format, ask and we will send it.

If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the German market surveillance authority for the accessibility of products and services ({de|Marktüberwachungsstelle der Länder für die Barrierefreiheit von Produkten und Dienstleistungen}).
